ticket.title: outfeed reserve exists in no tag, so no downstream project can install the command that is meant to replace its own script
ticket.description:
MEASURED 2026-11-12 from a downstream consumer (aerofoil), while deciding whether to replace its hand-written namespace-reservation script with `outfeed reserve` (their AF-22).

THE VERSION LAG
  `outfeed reserve` was added in d2f4df9 "feat(outfeed-core): add reserve check, scaffold and publish
  for namespace claims", committed 2026-11-05 22:16.
  `git tag --contains d2f4df9` returns nothing: the command is in no tag at all.
  crates.io `outfeed-cli` max_version is 0.1.0-beta.7, and that tree carries no reserve command -
  `git grep -i reserve v0.1.0-beta.7 -- '*.rs'` matches only unrelated code in clone.rs.
  The local checkout (HEAD 82e09fc) is 98 commits past its v0.1.0-beta.7 tag, which is why the verb
  works on a developer machine and nowhere else.

WHY IT BLOCKS A CONSUMER
aerofoil's scripts/reserve-namespaces.sh implements check/scaffold/publish in about 200 lines of
shell, including the crates.io 429 handling. AF-22 wants it reduced to a wrapper around this command,
and cannot: no installable outfeed has it. Unlike miter (GB-361), outfeed has no cross-repo path
dependency, so `cargo install --git https://github.com/gaugeblock/outfeed --rev <sha> outfeed-cli`
does work - the missing piece is purely a release, not a structural fix. AF-22 is parked on this.

TWO THINGS TO WEIGH WHILE CUTTING IT
  1. `reserve scaffold` takes names positionally and its `--repository` default is
     https://github.com/gaugeblock/{name} - the suite's own org. A consumer needs to pass a template
     for its own repository, and per-name overrides are already supported (`--repo-override NAME=URL`).
     Worth deciding whether a template alone is enough, or whether the default should be an error
     when it would point a placeholder at an org the caller does not own.
  2. There is no way to supply a description, so scaffolded placeholders carry a generic one.
     aerofoil's script carries a per-crate description for each name, and losing them is a (small)
     content regression that a wrapper would need to accept or the tool would need to support.

ACCEPTANCE
  * a published `outfeed-cli` version answers `outfeed reserve --help` with check, scaffold and publish;
  * `cargo install outfeed-cli --version <new> --locked` on a clean machine provides all three verbs;
  * the release's tag contains d2f4df9, so a consumer pinning the tag gets the verb.

NOT IN SCOPE
Changing what reservation does. This is about the same code being obtainable at the version a
consumer is told to run.
acceptance_criteria: a published outfeed-cli answers outfeed reserve --help with check, scaffold and publish
cargo install outfeed-cli --version <new> --locked on a clean machine provides all three verbs
the release tag contains d2f4df9, so a consumer pinning the tag gets the verb
